v99_restore_rejection_failsafe.root_cause: A rejected cross-entry semantic restore returned false without resetting reader-scroll, so a later non-ENTRY_START open could retain prior-entry pixel geometry after an interrupted/failed restore path.
v99_restore_rejection_failsafe.repair: When restoreSemanticReadingPosition returns false in the semantic-restore branch, reset reader-scroll to 0 immediately and on the next animation frame, then capture the new entry semantic position.

v100_navigation_target_failsafe.root_cause: After a failed cross-volume Search paragraph load, pendingSearchReaderTarget and pendingParaId could survive. A later unrelated non-ENTRY_START Reader open consumed the stale target; target focus found no matching fragment and left prior-entry pixel scroll geometry in place. The v99 semantic fallback also lacked a visible-reader identity token around its delayed animation-frame fallback, leaving a theoretical cross-navigation race.
v100_navigation_target_failsafe.repair: Identity-bind every delayed transient Reader target action to the visible volume/entry snapshot. Search target focus now returns success/failure; stale/missing Search or paragraph targets fail closed to the visible entry start. The semantic-rejection fallback is also identity-bound so it cannot reset a newer Reader after a navigation race.

v101_transactional_navigation_commit.root_cause: openEntryCore invalidated the visible Reader session and assigned currentVolume/back-origin before ensureVolumeReaderData completed. A failed cross-volume load therefore left the old entry visible while currentVolume already named the failed target and activeReaderSession was invalidated; pressing Next could navigate in the wrong Tome.
v101_transactional_navigation_commit.repair: Stage origin/back context, preload Reader data, resolve the requested entry/paragraph/supplement and validate a concrete target first. Only after target validation flush the prior Reader session, clear ENTRY_START transient state, and commit readerOriginContext, readerBack and currentVolume/currentEntry. A pre-commit load failure therefore leaves the old Reader identity/session untouched.

v102_transactional_supplement_target.root_cause: openSupplementItem flushed the visible Reader session and assigned currentSupplementFocusId/pendingParaId before openEntryCore could preload and validate the cross-volume target. If that load failed, the old entry remained visible but readerTargetIdentity could resolve to the failed supplement; a Favourite could then save the Tome-2 supplement with volume 12.
v102_transactional_supplement_target.repair: openSupplementItem now only derives an explicit navigationParaId and passes supplementId/target options into openEntry. It neither flushes the Reader session nor precommits supplement focus. openEntryCore uses the option for target resolution and commits pendingParaId/currentSupplementFocusId only after target preload/validation and session transition. Search and user-record supplement callers pass their explicit paragraph target through the option instead of global pre-mutation.
